item.title: Tuesday Night Figure Drawing - Open Studio — Tue Sep 29, 7:00 PM — the Space
item.description:
Every Tuesday, 7 – 9:30 pm at the Space | All skill levels welcome *Cover art by Ling Chen.
Tuesday night at The Space is your invitation to drop in, find your creative flow, and practice your drawing skills. Each week a different model – usually nude, and sometimes clothed – serves as our muse as we pursue creative expression through observation and mark making. We challenge how we see and what we want to say, observing the nuances of the human form, its moods, character, and light — and do our best to capture something in the moment that tells a story. This has become a supportive community of seekers, artists, experimenters, and curious souls drawn together by the shared pursuit of capturing the living human form. Use the time to refine your skills, experiment with different media, and deepen your understanding of anatomy, gesture, and proportion. item.title: Theater League of Clifton Announces Auditions for “1776” — Fri Oct 2, 7:00 PM
item.description: The Theater League of Clifton will hold auditions for its upcoming production of “1776” on Tuesday, September 15; Wednesday, September 16; and Thursday, September 17, from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Callbacks by invitation may also be held Thursday, September 17. Auditions will be held at Living Hope, 303 Maplewood Ave., Clifton, NJ 07013. Performances will be held November 13, 14 and 15 at the Wayne Community Center, 1 Pike Drive, Wayne, NJ. The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. With music and lyrics by Sherman Edwards and a book by Peter Stone, 1776 dramatizes the struggle within the Second Continental Congress to declare American independence. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort. item.title: Acrylic Pouring Workshop with Mohanima — Tue Oct 6, 1:00 PM — the Space
item.description:
Join us for an in-person, 1 day workshop where you will learn fluid art techniques for acrylic paints. This is a lively and fun, hands-on art making experience for all ages. Learn how to prepare your paints with various pouring mediums that when processed with a hair dryer, reveal the most unexpected and beautiful abstract art. Your teacher, Rakhi of Mohanima Art, will guide you through the whole process. You can watch videos of the process on her Instagram. Discussion on how to put a protective finish on your piece will also be covered. All materials will be provide so just bring your fabulous self. Each participant will create their own unique work of art. Tuesday, October 6, 1 – 4 pm Price: $150 (Incl all supplies) To purchase tickets go to their website page here – after signing up you will be taken to the ticket page to complete purchase.

item.title: AMERICAN HIGHER EDUCATION: FOUNDATION OF DEMOCRACY, ENGINE OF INNOVATION — Tue Oct 13, 2:30 PM — Cole Hall rm. 340
item.description: American higher education evolved from an elite system training clergy into a vital pillar of our democracy and economic progress. While the nation's Founders recognized the essential link between education and self-governance, contemporary universities did not initially serve this broader public purpose. The first dramatic shift came during the Civil War, when the Morrill Act of 1862 established land-grant universities with a public mission to train citizens in building the infrastructure and agricultural capacity of a developing nation. This democratic commitment expanded over the decades to include African Americans through the 1890 Morrill Act and to train educators via normal schools, like Montclair, at the turn of the century. Following World War II, the "Endless Frontier" report permanently linked university research with national security and industrial strength. item.title: The Balanced Woman Blueprint: Wellness Reset for Women 40+ — Sat Oct 24, 10:00 AM — the Space
item.description:
RESET is a two-hour wellness experience designed for women 40+ who are ready to stop running on autopilot and start making intentional decisions about what comes next.
Saturday, October 24, 10am – 12noon, $45 Get clear about what you want. Make bold decisions about what comes next. Leave with a practical plan to reclaim your life. You’ve spent years showing up for your career, your family, your relationships, and the people who depend on you. You’re capable. You’re responsible. You get things done. But somewhere along the way, you may have become the last person on your own list. And maybe you’re asking yourself:
What do I actually want now? What needs to change?
